item.title: Lower and upper solutions for boundary value problems with bounded $\Phi$-laplacian Stieltjes-differential inclusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of solutions between given lower and upper solutions for several types of boundary value problems involving bounded Phi-Laplacian inclusions. We consider derivatives in the Stieltjes sense, that is, derivatives with respect to nondecreasing and left-continuous functions. This framework includes, as particular cases, both differential and difference equations, even allowing for impulses at the discontinuity points of the derivator. To the best of the authors knowledge, this paper presents the first application of the method of lower and upper solutions to second-order boundary value problems with Stieltjes derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Lopez Pouso, Paula Vazquez Garcia

item.title: Endpoint Exclusion for Bounded Damping on the Standard Flat Two-Torus
item.description: arXiv:2611.26631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for every fixed nonzero nonnegative bounded damping $W$ on the standard flat two-torus, the stationary damped wave operator satisfies $\|(-\Delta-s^2+isW)^{-1}\|_{L^2\to L^2}=o(|s|)$. Consequently, for initial data in $H^2\times H^1$, the uniform decay rate of the square root of the energy improves from $O(t^{-1/2})$ to $o(t^{-1/2})$. This excludes the endpoint quasimodes proposed by Kleinhenz in 2024. The proof combines a uniform $L^4$ estimate, equidistribution of densities when the largest Fourier coefficient tends to zero, and a one-dimensional equation for a nonzero modulated weak limit. No continuity of the damping is required. The improvement may depend on $W$ and does not assert a fixed gain in the polynomial exponent.
item.dc:creator: Zikang Deng

item.title: Symmetry, boundary conditions, and the Noether correspondence of the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.26632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conserved quantities of nonlinear dispersive wave equations are typically derived on the whole plane, whereas numerical simulations evaluate them on a torus. We examine how compactifying one or both spatial directions affects the Noether correspondences of the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation, obtained from its potential Lagrangian, on the family of domains $\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{T}\}^2$. The outcome is a three-valued classification: intrinsic, chart-dependent, or defective. Only the two first moments, whose characteristics carry an undifferentiated coordinate weight, are affected. A moment can become defective only if its weighted direction is compact and the mass flux crosses the seam of the chosen fundamental domain; for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation this happens exactly for the longitudinal moment when $x$ is compact. The status of each moment depends only on the boundary condition along its weighted direction. When $x$ is compact, the Galilean boost still maps solutions to solutions, but no global Noether charge corresponds to it.
item.dc:creator: Yuichiro Shimazaki

item.title: Nonexistence of $(1,6)$-sign soliton solutions for the damped nonlinear Klein--Gordon equation in 2D
item.description: arXiv:2611.26635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the two-dimensional damped nonlinear Klein--Gordon equation $$\begin{align*} \partial_t^2u-\Delta u+2\alpha\partial_tu+u-|u|^{p-1}u=0 \end{align*}$$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $\alpha>0$ and $p>2$. We study multi-soliton solutions asymptotic in the energy space, in the full-time limit $t\to\infty$, to a superposition of translated ground states, with one soliton having the sign opposite to that of the other $k$ solitons. C\^{o}te and Du conjectured nonexistence for $k\geq7$ in the regular polygonal setting and identified the hexagonal case $k=6$ as critical. In this paper, we prove that $(1,k)$-sign soliton solutions do not exist for any $k\geq6$, without imposing any symmetry assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Kenjiro Ishizuka

item.title: Overview and recent progress on the classical Bernoulli free boundary problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.26636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This survey gives an overview of the Bernoulli or one-phase free boundary problem, with emphasis on recent progress.
item.dc:creator: Xavier Fern\'andez-Real

item.title: Boundary remainders and optimal convergence rates for planar spectral partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S_m(\Omega)$ denote the infimum of the sum of the first Dirichlet eigenvalues over partitions of a bounded connected planar domain $\Omega$ into exactly $m$ nonempty connected open cells. We study the convergence of $|\Omega|S_m(\Omega)/m^2$ to its universal limit $c_*$. If the full topological boundary has zero area, we bound the absolute error by the area of its tubular neighborhood at scale $m^{-1/2}$, together with an $O(m^{-1/2})$ term. This yields rates $O_\Omega(m^{-1/2})$ on Lipschitz domains and $O_\Omega(m^{-\alpha/2})$ on domains with finitely many $C^{0,\alpha}$ boundary charts, $0<\alpha<1$, for all sufficiently large integers. The square and a fixed smooth domain have positive matching lower bounds of order $m^{-1/2}$. For each $\alpha\in(0,1)$, a fixed H\"older graph domain attains the order $m^{-\alpha/2}$ along a subsequence. Little H\"older domains satisfy the corresponding little-$o$ estimate, but no prescribed additional factor tending to zero works for the whole class, even with domain-dependent constants. An auxiliary energy with variable cell count gives the boundary estimate; a positive correction on the square and sparse graph constructions yield the lower bounds.
item.dc:creator: Yufan Cen

item.title: Almost sure scattering for the energy-critical Hartree equation with radial data below the energy space
item.description: arXiv:2611.26639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the energy-critical Hartree equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge5$, with randomized radial initial data of supercritical regularity. To handle the nonlocal Hartree interaction, we exploit the Riesz smoothing of the Hartree convolution through a bilinear decomposition adapted to the regularity of the interacting terms. This leads to a Hartree bilinear estimate that allows us to combine probabilistic weighted spacetime estimates with weighted and interaction Morawetz estimates. For every $d\ge5$, we establish almost sure local well-posedness for randomized radial data below the energy regularity, together with a conditional scattering criterion. For $d\ge7$, we further prove almost sure global existence and scattering. The uniform energy and Morawetz bounds are established through a double bootstrap argument combining the Hartree bilinear decomposition with an energy increment estimate.
item.dc:creator: Yuli Feng, Yuyang Ye, Han Yang

item.title: Corrigendum to "Sparse Gabor representations of metaplectic operators: controlled exponential decay and Schr\"odinger confinement" [Adv. Math. 490 (2026) 110828]
item.description: arXiv:2611.26642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this note is to correct some quantitative estimates and computations in [Adv. Math. 490 (2026) 110828]. The proofs of Theorem 1.3 and Lemma 3.6 there contain gaps, and consequently some of the numerical decay coefficients that depend on them need adjustment. Some identities concerning Hamiltonian flows and Euler decompositions in Section 6 also require correction. Theorem 1.2 and the qualitative conclusions of the general metaplectic estimates in [Adv. Math. 490 (2026) 110828], namely Gabor sparsity and exponential confinement for quadratic Schr\"odinger evolutions, are not affected.
item.dc:creator: Elena Cordero, Gianluca Giacchi, Edoardo Pucci, Salvatore Ivan Trapasso

item.title: Eigenvalues and Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator in the Large-Friction Limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.26664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator by the methods of analytic dilation and phase-space deformation. We prove that in the large-friction limit $\gamma\to+\infty$, there are neither eigenvalues nor resonances away from the thresholds $\gamma N$, and that near each threshold $\gamma k$, there exists a bijection between the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and those of the Witten Laplacian at the level $k$, $-\Delta_V^{(k)}=-\Delta_V\otimes 1_{\mu_k}-d\Gamma_k(\operatorname{Hess}V)$. We also show that each negative eigenvalue of $-\Delta_V^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, produces a pole of the resolvent at distance of order $\gamma^{-1}$ below $\gamma k$, whose imaginary part is $O(e^{-c\gamma})$ for every $c<2\delta_V$. Here $\delta_V$ is the width of a strip of analyticity of $V$.
item.dc:creator: Xue Ping Wang (LMJL)

item.title: The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area
item.description: arXiv:2611.26729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Phi(P)=|P|\mu_1(P)$, where $\mu_1(P)$ is the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of $P$. For every $N\ge3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes $\Phi$, up to congruence, among simple polygons of fixed area with at most $N$ sides. The values $\Phi(R_N)$ increase strictly with $N$. The maximization theorem answers Laugesen's question \cite[Problem~(1), p.~405]{ABLW} and proves the polygonal Szeg\H{o}--Weinberger conjecture of Laugesen and Siudeja \cite[Conjecture~6.36]{LSH}. It also implies that the triangular lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of the Voronoi cell at fixed covolume.
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo, Bingbing Xie

item.title: An Optimal Liouville Theorem for the Fully Fractional Heat Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.26767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every nonnegative entire classical solution of the fully fractional heat equation $(\partial_t-\Delta)^s u=u^p$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ is identically zero for $n\geq2$, $0<s<1$, and $1<p<(n+2s)/(n-2s)$. No global boundedness, decay, or symmetry assumptions are required for the solutions. The exponent range is sharp, since the critical equation admits positive stationary solutions. Our result provides a fractional counterpart of Quittner's optimal Liouville theorem for the classical semilinear heat equation, while our proof follows a new and simpler approach. For bounded solutions, we combine elliptic nonexistence and compactness to control superlevel set measures by the local energy dissipation of the weighted extension. A local energy inequality then gives nonexistence by iteration. Doubling, local regularity, and a nonlocal convergence theorem yield a universal pointwise bound in terms of the parabolic distance to the boundary, which implies our Liouville theorem for general solutions.
item.dc:creator: Yahong Guo, Yugao Ouyang, Jiongduo Xie

item.title: Finite-Time Singularity Formation for the Three-Dimensional Euler Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.26772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time. The velocity remains bounded, while the vorticity magnitude at the origin tends to infinity. Away from the origin, the velocity and its time derivative have smooth spatial limits at the singular time. The construction uses localized Craik--Criminale waves as building blocks of a multi-scale construction.
item.dc:creator: Levent Alp\"oge, Tristan Buckmaster, Matei P. Coiculescu

item.title: The double-endpoint Strichartz estimate for dispersion-managed Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.26850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We adapt the near-far argument of Hadama and Toyoshima to establish the double-endpoint Strichartz estimate for dispersion-managed Schr\"odinger equations.
item.dc:creator: Jason Murphy, Jiqiang Zheng

item.title: Hypocoercivity estimates via maximum principle in short and long time scales
item.description: arXiv:2611.26851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove decay estimates for a large class of linear drift-diffusion operators with hypoelliptic structure. In the main example, the diffusion consists of (possibly superposing) local or nonlocal operators acting on a restricted set of variables, while diffusivity is transported to the whole space thanks to H\"ormander-type conditions on the drift term. We prove both short-time and long-time oscillation estimates on the solutions, including bounded-to-Lipschitz smoothing in the sharp time scale and exponential decay, as time goes to infinity, whenever a strict supersolution, with the role of Lyapunov function, is supposed to exist. The estimates are proved with a unifying approach relying on doubling variables and coupling methods, using maximum principle in suitably time scaled moving frames. Applications range from nonlocal kinetic Fokker-Planck equations to heat conduction models in a chain of coupled oscillators.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Porretta, Davide Francesco Redaelli

item.title: A dynamic variational principle on phase space for Wasserstein cubic splines
item.description: arXiv:2611.26862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wasserstein cubic splines have been introduced to provide a smooth interpolation in time between prescribed probability measures on $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Their construction for $N$ measures is based on a multi-marginal optimal transport problem on a space of dimension $N\! \cdot \! d$, thus becoming very high-dimensional already for a small number of prescribed measures. We prove that the dimension can be reduced to a fixed number $2d+1$ via a dynamic variational principle on phase space. We also give an example showing that the Monge ansatz, which would also reduce the dimension to a fixed number, fails to capture exact solutions and is in general ill-posed, even for absolutely continuous measures.
item.dc:creator: Gero Friesecke, Daniel Matthes

item.title: Finite propagation speed for evolutionary equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.26876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite speed of propagation in the framework of evolutionary equations introduced by Rainer Picard in 2009. We establish sufficient conditions on the material law, which is represented by an analytic and bounded operator-valued function, and the unbounded spatial operator that ensure finite speed of propagation of information for solutions. Assuming a linear-in-frequency coercivity bound for spatially local material laws, we prove propagation on backward light cones for weighted $L_2$ solutions without a finite initial time, thus identifying hyperbolic-type evolutionary equations. The characteristic-speed threshold depends on the coercive coefficient and the principal spatial matrices, but not on bounded memory or delay terms or potential positive fractional temporal contributions. We illustrate the result with the scalar wave equation, Maxwell's equations, a fractional model in elasticity, and dual-phase-lag thermoelasticity.
item.dc:creator: Joseline Simo Tekeu, Marcus Waurick

item.title: On a potential type II singular model of the Navier Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.26898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that a particular class of partial type I or type II functions are not singularity models for the three dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with or without smooth, compactly supported forces. This extends part of the results for the axially symmetric case to the full three dimension case. Some connections to the recent literature are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Qi S. Zhang

item.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian quotient equations on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.26964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the Dirichlet problem for a class of sum Hessian quotient equations involving a gradient term on the right-hand side on Riemannian manifolds. Under the assumption of the existence of a subsolution, based on the a priori estimates for the solutions, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of $(k-1)$-admissible solutions for the Dirichlet problem on compact Riemannian manifolds with smooth boundary. Our existence results cover the case $0\le l<k<n$ with $k\ge 2$, where the subsolution is assumed to be $(k-1)$-admissible, and the case $k=n$ with $0\le l\le n-2$, where the subsolution is assumed to be $n$-admissible.
item.dc:creator: Guanghan Li, Chenyang Liu

item.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.
item.dc:creator: Jinbing Chen, Colin Grant, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky

item.title: Long-time existence for wave systems with derivative nonlinearities
item.description: arXiv:2611.27078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study wave systems with power-type derivative nonlinearities in space dimensions $n\geq3$, for small, spherically symmetric initial data. Under suitable assumptions on the nonlinear powers, we establish global existence and sharp lifespan lower bounds. To achieve this, we develop weighted energy and local energy estimates adapted to the null directions, together with corresponding pointwise decay estimates.
item.dc:creator: Wei Dai, Mengyun Liu, Chengbo Wang

item.title: Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for Radial Compressible Navier-Stokes Flow with Density-Dependent Viscosities on a Disk and in the Plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.27108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations admit a unique global strong solution for arbitrarily large radial initial data without swirl, both on a disk with a no-slip wall and in the whole plane. On the disk we require the initial acceleration to have zero trace at the wall. The initial density is bounded away from zero and, in the plane, approaches a positive constant at infinity. The shear and second viscosities have a common density exponent between one half and one, inclusive. Throughout the strictly dissipative range of viscosity coefficients, every pressure exponent greater than or equal to one is admissible. In particular, the result applies to Marche's viscous shallow water equations on a flat bottom in the absence of rotation, bottom friction, and capillarity. These equations retain the positive second viscosity derived from free-surface flow and thus fall outside the Bresch-Desjardins relation. The density stays bounded above and away from zero uniformly in time. On the disk, the density converges exponentially to its spatial mean and the velocity to zero in the Sobolev norm of order three. In the plane, convergence in the same norm holds to the prescribed far-field state. The argument also applies to a class of non-power viscosity laws.
item.dc:creator: Kexin Li

item.title: Weak-strong uniqueness for the Landau equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the spatially inhomogeneous Landau equation with soft potentials, including the Coulomb case. Let $f$ and $g$ be nonnegative, uniformly continuous distributional solutions on $[0,T]$ with the same initial data. We prove that $f=g$ on $[0,T]$ if both solutions have sufficient polynomial decay in velocity and the diffusion matrix of $f$ satisfies the usual anisotropic lower bound. For weak solutions, this proves a stronger form of \cite[Conjecture~1.4]{HW}, with no prescribed modulus of continuity for the initial datum. The proof is by duality. We obtain a weighted $L^2$ estimate for the velocity Hessian of the solution to a backward adjoint equation. In the second-order nonlocal term, we write $g$ as the sum of its velocity mollification and a remainder. Uniform continuity makes the remainder small. For the mollified part, two integrations by parts give a bound proportional to the length of the time interval.
item.dc:creator: Weinan Wang

item.title: Conservative Implicit and Explicit Solvers for Reactive Conformable Transport with Multirate Memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.27318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we analyze conservative implicit and explicit schemes for reactive transport with a conformable time scale and multirate exchange. The conformable derivative defines a local change of time coordinate, while exchange with immobile regions supplies the memory. Positive Gauss--Jacobi quadrature approximates the prescribed exchange spectrum by finite compartments. Both schemes use conservative finite-volume fluxes. Forward Euler gives the explicit update; backward Euler initializes the implicit second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2). Eliminating the compartment states reduces each implicit step to a tridiagonal system. Under stated mesh and regularity conditions, we prove implicit solvability, conditional explicit positivity and stability, and discrete mass balance. A cell-average error estimate separates spatial, compartment and temporal contributions. Its proof accounts for the boundary fluxes and the BDF2 startup error. Source-specific bounds make the temporal and memory prefactors uniform under mesh and compartment refinement. For a broader positive-history model, continuous residual estimates have coefficients independent of memory strength and kernel mass. Local coercivity gives a sharper coefficient. Manufactured tests recover second-order spatial convergence, first-order Euler convergence and second-order BDF2 convergence. Separate experiments examine the memory and combined estimates. In a prescribed porous-medium application, the finest numerical states differ by $3.57\times10^{-5}$ in relative space--time $L^2$. Independent resolution checks support the computed pulse attenuation, immobile storage and release after injection ends.
item.dc:creator: Zahraa Abdallah, Hayman Thabet

item.title: Very weak solutions of nonlinear elliptic systems with Orlicz growth
item.description:
arXiv:2611.27385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we consider non-linear elliptic equations with respect to Orlicz growth, for instance equations of the form $$ \mathrm{div}(\varphi(\vert 
abla u \vert) 
abla u)= 0. $$ We study very weak solutions to this system, that is, solutions that are not a priori in the correct energy space to this equation ($\varphi(\vert 
abla u \vert) \vert 
abla u \vert^2 \in L^1$). On the one hand, using rather mild assumptions on the corresponding Orlicz space (we need either the $\Delta_2$ or $
abla_2$ condition, but not both at the same time), we can show that the integrability of very weak solutions improves to the energy space, provided that the initial integrability is close enough to the energy space. On the other hand, mirroring the construction of Colombo and Tione (Non-classical solutions of the $p$-Laplace equation, J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2024), for the $p$-Laplacian, we give a construction of 'wild' solutions for a $L \log L$-type Laplacian.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Schiffer, Akram Sharif

item.title: Boundary concentration and Pohozaev identity for the fractional p-Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.27394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Pohozaev-like identity for bounded weak solutions of the fractional p-Laplace equation with a locally Lipschitz nonlinearity on bounded C^2 domains, provided that s>max{1/2-1/p,0}. We compare the weak equations for the solution and its spatial deformation to show that the first-order contribution of the energy remainder is concentrated at the boundary. The boundary term involves the weighted trace, with a coefficient expressed by an integral of the one-dimensional boundary profile.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Ortega

item.title: Gradient Stability of the Morrey and Hardy inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2611.27450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find that the quantitative gradient stability estimate for the Morrey inequality in a ball $B_R$ fails with respect to any exponent of the {\it gradient-level} distance $D_M(u):=\inf\{\|\nabla u-\nabla v\|_{L^p(B_R)}:v\in \mathcal{M}\}$. Instead, the estimate holds with $D_M(u^\star),$ the gradient-level distance between the Schwarz symmetrization $u^\star$ and the space of Morrey extremals $\mathcal{M}$. Nevertheless, we establish a gradient stability estimate for the Morrey inequality by slightly `weakening' the above distance. We also obtain analogous gradient stability for the geometric $L^p$-Hardy inequality in certain domains. Distinct behaviors in the stability of these two inequalities have been discussed. Furthermore, in the $L^2$-case, we investigate the optimal constants and their attainability in both the Morrey and Hardy gradient stability inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Ujjal Das, Subhajit Roy

item.title: A 2D Free Boundary Model for Atherosclerosis with Diffusion and Elasticity
item.description: arXiv:2611.27451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a coupled elasticity--diffusion model on a deformable domain to describe the interaction between diffusion and mechanical deformation. We first study the two-dimensional formulation and investigate its numerical behavior. A quasi-stationary formulation is then derived, and a linear relation between the total mass of the diffusing species and the volume change of the domain is established. Next, a one-dimensional reduction is introduced as a particular case of the two-dimensional model to provide additional analytical insight into the coupled dynamics. Finally, the proposed framework is applied to a model of atherosclerosis, where numerical simulations illustrate the influence of the model parameters on inflammatory wave propagation and arterial wall deformation.
item.dc:creator: Ghada Abi Younes, Nader El Khatib, Nicolai Bessonov, Vitaly Volpert

item.title: Boundary gradient asymptotics for superquadratic viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations via optimal control
item.description: arXiv:2611.27484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the boundary behavior of the maximal solution of \[ -\Delta u + |\nabla u|^{p} + \lambda u = f \] on arbitrary bounded $C^{2}$ domains, where $p > 2$ and $\lambda > 0$. For bounded state-dependent terms $f$, we resolve a conjecture of Lasry and Lions by establishing sharp boundary gradient asymptotics without geometric restrictions on the domain. Previously, such asymptotics were established only for certain classes of domains with additional restrictions on $p$ and $f$. We also extend the analysis to state-dependent terms that may be singular near the boundary and obtain sharp boundary profiles and gradient asymptotics. Our approach relies on stochastic optimal control and boundary blow-up analysis. Dynamic programming estimates and comparisons of near-optimal trajectories establish tangential invariance of boundary blow-up limits, leading to the identification of one-dimensional profiles and the asymptotic formulas. For the associated state-constrained control problem, we establish sharp asymptotics for the minimizing feedback and deduce its admissibility and optimality, with corresponding results for the ergodic problem.
item.dc:creator: S. E. Nikitin

item.title: Global Critical $L^3$ Well-Posedness for the Stochastic Tamed Navier--Stokes Equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with Wiener and Jump Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.27493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the global well-posedness for the three dimensional stochastic tamed Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with multiplicative Wiener and compensated Poisson noise. When noise coefficients are globally Lipschitz on $L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)$ and satisfy spatial $H^1_\sigma$ regularity assumptions, the system admits a pathwise unique global, probabilistically strong, critical mild solution for any initial datum $u_0 \in L^0(\Omega, \mathcal F_0; L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)) $. Neither smallness nor moment or finite kinetic energy assumptions on $u_0$ are required. We also establish that the global solution depends continuously in probability on the initial datum in uniform-in-time $L^3$ and space-time $L^5$ norms on every finite time interval.
item.dc:creator: Bikram Podder, Surendra Kumar

item.title: Solutions with one dimensional concentration for a two dimensional Schr\"odinger model with general potential and involving mass subcritical and supercritical exponents
item.description: arXiv:2611.27498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of solution $(\tilde u, \lambda)$ which concentrates on stationary and non-degenerate curve, as $p_\epsilon \to 6$, to the following mass-constraint nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \begin{align*} \begin{cases} - \Delta \tilde u + W({\bf y}) \tilde u - |\tilde u|^{p_\epsilon-2} \tilde u = \lambda \tilde u, \quad {\bf y} \in \mathbb{R}^2, \\[2mm] \int_{\R^2} |\tilde u|^2 {\mathrm d} {\bf y} =a. \end{cases} \end{align*} Here $\lambda$ is a Lagrange multiplier, $ W({\bf y})$ is a real-valued potential, $a \in \mathbb{R}_+$ is a constant, $p_\epsilon = 6 \pm \epsilon, \epsilon \ll 1$ and $6$ is the $L^2$-critical exponent in the sense of concentration on a codimension 1 submanifold. When constructing the solution concentrating on a curve, we utilize some delicate transformations to overcome the challenges posed by the non-uniform boundedness of length of concentrating curves. In addition, we employ some refined analytical techniques to overcome the strong resonance phenomena caused by the $L^2$ constraint. Our result partially answers the Ambrosetti-Malchiodi-Ni conjecture in the setting of the mass-constrained nonlinear elliptic equation.
item.dc:creator: Lipeng Duan, Suting Wei, Jun Yang

item.title: Approximating technique for the solution to the ${H}^{\infty}$ -optimal control problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.27520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper continues the results published in [G. Marinoschi, Appl. Math. Optimiz. 94:44, 1-29, 2026], by presenting an approximating method of calculating the solution to the $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem, which solves the robust stabilization of a system by a feedback controller, and to the associated Riccati equation. This method generates a sequence of infinite dimensional systems approximating the original system and the solution to the approximating $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem is proved to converge to the solution of the original $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem. An example for calculating the solution to the Riccati equation and the feedback controller is provided at the end.
item.dc:creator: Gabriela Marinoschi

item.title: Uniqueness of $L_{p}$ Minkowski Problem in the supercritical range near the affine exponent
item.description: arXiv:2611.27558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the isotropic $ L_{p} $-Minkowski problem. The equation is affine invariant at the exponent $ p = -n-1 $, where all origin-centered ellipsoids with the volume of the unit ball are solutions, and it is known that the unit sphere is the only solution for $ p \in (-n-1, 1) $. We prove uniform $ C^{0} $ estimates for all solutions in the supercritical range $ p < -n-1 $. This allows us to prove a key spectral estimate of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator on solutions. We then utilize the Rayleigh quotient method with position vectors as test functions for the operator adapted from Ivaki-Milman to prove uniqueness in the range $ p \in (-n-1- \delta_{n}, -n-1) $ for some $ \delta_{n} > 0 $.
item.dc:creator: Devesh Rajpal

item.title: Local well-posedness for generalized inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.dc:creator: Kohei Inada

item.title: The Global Solutions to Nonlinear Thermoelastic Systems under a Null Condition
item.description: arXiv:2611.27629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for a class of homogeneous, isotropic nonlinear thermoelastic systems in three space dimensions. Under a null condition for purely elastic part of our system which is different from those considered by Sideris, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global classical solutions with smallness assumptions on the initial data. We use Klainerman--Sideris weighted energy estimates and time-weighted energy estimates for the heat equation to establish global existence. Moreover, we improve upon the global existence result of Ponce and Racke, who assumed that the purely elastic nonlinear terms vanish.
item.dc:creator: Yating Xu, Yi Zhou

item.title: Global existence and scattering of large solutions of the cubic Dirac equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct global dispersive solutions to the massive cubic Dirac equation (Soler Model) for initial data with large critical Sobolev norm. Because of a lack of a coercive energy in the Dirac equation, the only previously known large solutions are solitons (which are non-dispersive) and Majorana-solutions (which are in fact solutions to a linear equation). Here, the new strategy is to exploit the non-relativistic limit, which connects the Dirac equation to a system of Schr\"odinger equations with cubic nonlinearities, and then to develop a scattering theory for this limiting system.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Candy, Sebastian Herr, Kenji Nakanishi

item.title: Approximation of the Nonautonomous Maxwell System with an Interface
item.description: arXiv:2611.27676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To obtain higher-regularity solutions for nonautonomous Maxwell systems with an interface, we approximate the initial data and coefficients by smoother counterparts. To preserve compatibility conditions of the approximations, required to obtain solutions to the Maxwell systems, we systematically adjust the approximating sequence of initial data. While the existing well-posedness theory in [14] guarantees more regular solutions, standard a-priori estimates fail to ensure convergence in the desired norm. We overcome this by a mollification argument and a div-curl estimate from [4] and [7].
item.dc:creator: Richard Nutt

item.title: Small noise limit for Entropic Variational Mean-Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.27695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study second order variational mean-field games with quadratic Hamiltonian. In analogy with entropic optimal transport, Benamou, Carlier, Di Marino and the second author recently proposed an entropy-minimization formulation of the problem, which could be interpreted as the Lagrangian counterpart of the classical Eulerian approach. We investigate the small-noise $\Gamma$-limit for the Lagrangian entropy-minimization formulation and establish $\Gamma$-convergence of second order mean-field games towards their deterministic first order counterpart. This also translates into another (dynamical) proof of the convergence of the Schr\"odinger problem to optimal transport. Moreover, we study the original Eulerian problem and prove a first order energy expansion, which establishes a selection principle for minimizers of the deterministic problem.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Cosenza, Luca Nenna

item.title: Exponential decay of the quasilinear Maxwell system caused by conductivity on a collar
item.description: arXiv:2611.27733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the anisotropic, quasilinear Maxwell system on a bounded domain $\Omega$ with perfectly conducting boundary conditions. It is damped via a conductivity $\sigma$ which is strictly positive on its support containing a collar of the boundary. We prove that solutions exist globally and decay exponentially to $0$ if there are no magnetic charges on $\Omega$, no electric charges off the support of $\sigma$, and the initial fields are small. Our approach relies on a splitting of the solution via adapted Helmholtz decompositions and an observability-type estimate for a related system without charges, shown by means of Morawetz multipliers. Moreover, one has to control the space derivatives of the solution by its time derivatives, exploiting the structure of the system. The discontinuity of $\sigma$ introduces an interface which poses significant challenges in all these steps, besides those coming from the quasilinear terms.
item.dc:creator: Richard Nutt, Roland Schnaubelt

item.title: Weakly competing bubbles for a critical elliptic system in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the critical competitive system $$\left\{\begin{array}{ll} -\Delta u=u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}}+\beta u^{\frac{2}{n-2}}v^{\frac{n}{n-2}}, & \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n,\\ -\Delta v=v^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}}+\beta v^{\frac{2}{n-2}}u^{\frac{n}{n-2}}, & \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n. \end{array}\right.$$ where $p=\frac{n+2}{n-2}$, $q=\frac{2}{n-2}$ and $\beta<0$. In dimensions three and four, solutions combining a bubble in one component with a ring of bubbles in the other have been constructed by Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. For $n\ge5$ this approach breaks down: the coupling is sublinear, the energy is only of class $C^1$, and small corrections cannot be kept away from the region where the nonlinearity is singular. We overcome this obstruction with a variational reduction in the spirit of Bahri and Rey, in which the infinite-dimensional correction is obtained by constrained minimization and is only required to depend continuously on the parameters. The resulting finite-dimensional problem is then solved by a degree argument. In this way, for every $n\ge5$ and every integer $k\ge2$, we construct nonnegative finite-energy solutions in the weak-competition regime $\beta\to0^-$: the first component is close to a standard bubble, while the second concentrates at the $k$ vertices of a regular polygon. The concentration scale is $d_*\varepsilon(1+o(1))$, with $d_*$ explicit and $\varepsilon^{(n-4)/2}=|\beta|\,|\ln\varepsilon|$, and we give precise expansions of the amplitudes and of the remainders.
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Ceresa Dussel, Maria Medina, Angela Pistoia

item.title: On the fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic quenching problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.27774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic free boundary problem $$|Du|^\kappa F(D^2u)-u_t=u^{\gamma-1} \qquad \textrm{in} \quad \{u>0\},$$ where $\kappa>0$, $0<\gamma<1$, and $F$ is a convex or concave uniformly elliptic operator with $F(0)=0$. We establish the existence of a nonnegative viscosity solution with prescribed continuous nonnegative boundary data and prove its optimal upper growth along the free boundary, together with matching non-degeneracy estimates in parabolic cylinders adapted to the scaling. Our approach combines a weak Bernstein estimate with barrier arguments to obtain local compactness and boundary attainment. To obtain the optimal growth rate, we further use persistence of positivity for limits with vanishing absorption coefficients to identify the homogeneous equation across the zero set, and then combine the optimal spatial regularity estimate of \cite{LLYZ25} with an iteration argument.
item.dc:creator: Seunghyun Kim, Jos\'{e} Miguel Urbano

item.title: Elliptic regularization for anisotropic mean curvature flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.27789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an elliptic regularization scheme for anisotropic mean curvature flow in arbitrary dimension, with general norms serving as surface tension and mobility. Starting from a non-fattening set of finite perimeter, we prove that the vertically rescaled minimizers and translating solitons converge in the Kuratowski sense to the unique generalized level-set motion, and locally in BV to the flat flow. Furthermore, by implementing a restarting and matching procedure prior to curvature identification, we establish for the limit flat flow a coupled phase-transport and surface-energy dissipation balance valid for arbitrary, possibly crystalline, anisotropies. When the surface tension is continuously differentiable (away from the origin) and strictly convex, we further prove that the flat flow is a BV flow and that its reduced boundary defines a unit-density anisotropic Brakke flow. To our knowledge, this is the first construction of unit-density anisotropic Brakke flows valid for every strictly convex differentiable surface tension, in arbitrary dimension and for prescribed non-fattening initial data, without assuming perimeter convergence.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Alberto Antonini, Antonio De Rosa, Massimiliano Morini, Salvatore Stuvard

item.title: Compactness from fractional momentum bounds and weak solutions of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.27830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the barotropic Navier--Stokes equations on ${\mathbb R}^3$ with constant viscosities, finite mass and finite energy. For every $\gamma>1$, a local bound on the momentum $m=\rho u$ in $L^2_tH^{-1+\sigma}_x$, $\sigma>0$, gives strong local convergence of the densities under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1. For $\gamma>9/8$ we prove, uniformly along the approximations, $$ \|I_{1-\alpha}m\|_{L^2(I\times{\mathbb R}^3)}\leq C_{I,\alpha} \qquad\text{for some }\alpha>0,\quad I\Subset(0,\infty).$$ Here $I_s$ is the spatial Riesz potential. Together with tightness of the energy at spatial infinity, this gives a global finite-energy renormalized weak solution.
item.dc:creator: Yanlin Liu, Ping Zhang
