item.dc:creator: Giacomo Vizzari

item.title: A sharp dimensional threshold for polygonal bubbling in an almost critical problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.27859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study sign-changing solutions for the problem $-\Delta u=|u|^{2^*-2-\varepsilon}u$ in $\mathcal B$, $u=0$ on $\partial\mathcal B$, where $\mathcal B$ is the unit ball of $\mathbb R^N$, $N\geq3$, $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter, so that the problem is slightly subcritical. In \cite{BDP}, Bartsch, D'Aprile and Pistoia proved that, in every dimension, there exist two solutions which blow up, as $\varepsilon\to0$, positively at the origin and negatively at two antipodal points; as a by-product of our approach, we prove their conjecture that the corresponding reduced energy has exactly two critical points, both nondegenerate, in every dimension. We consider the natural generalization in which the negative bubbles are located at the vertices of a regular $k$-gon, $k\geq3$, and we show that the picture changes drastically. When $k=3$ there is a sharp dimensional threshold: if $N\geq13$ the reduced energy has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate saddle point and a nondegenerate local minimum, which generate two distinct solutions, while if $3\leq N\leq12$ no solution of this type exists. When $k\geq4$ no solution of this type exists in any dimension. Moreover, for both families of solutions found for $k=3$ the nodal set stays uniformly away from $\partial\mathcal B$, in contrast with the case of two negative bubbles, where the nodal set of one of the two solutions touches the boundary, and with the Brezis--Nirenberg problem, where the nodal set of the solutions with the same configuration always reaches the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Mario Rago, Giusi Vaira, Yue Wu

item.title: On the long-time behaviour and asymptotic geometry of nonlocal aggregation equations with saturating mobility
item.description: arXiv:2611.27872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional nonlocal conservation law with a saturating Lipschitz mobility, without assuming concavity of the mobility. For attractive radial potentials, we establish global entropy well-posedness and exact mass confinement. When the interaction potential is quadratic on the active interaction zone of the solution, the nonlocal convolution reduces to an affine drift. This reduction bounds the total path length of the moving barycentre via macroscopic energy dissipation, establishing strong $L^1$ relative compactness of the trajectory through a late-time core-filling approximation that traps the entropic state via $L^1$ contraction, circumventing the imposition of a uniform bounded variation estimate. This compactness, combined with the energy dissipation, forces the entropic trajectory to converge strongly in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ as $t \to \infty$ to a unique stationary binary state. We characterize the geometry of this limit, proving an equivalence with measure-theoretically star-shaped sets. We demonstrate that the nonlocal dynamics admit non-circular stationary equilibria and do not select a unique saturated disk absent radial symmetry on the initial datum. Finally, for entropic stationary binary states of finite perimeter, we exclude essentially bounded measure-theoretic components of the support complement under strict subharmonicity of the interaction potential, and rule out positively separated support components under uniform convexity.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Perugini, Emanuela Radici

item.title: On the interplay between the anisotropy and the regularity of the coefficients in non autonomous problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.27877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the local Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers of non autonomous integral {functionals} of the form \begin{equation*} \label{functional} {\mathcal{F}(z) =} \int_\Omega F(x, Dz)\,dx, \end{equation*} where $\Omega$ is a bounded open set of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 2$ and the energy density $F(x,\xi)$ satisfies general growth conditions with respect to the gradient variable. The main novelty of this work lies in the identification of a suitable condition on the interplay between the regularity of the partial map $x\to {F(x,\xi)}$ and the ratio of the non uniform ellipticity of the problem that is sufficient to obtain the Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers. Our result extends and unifies those previously known from the literature, including the standard $p-$growth case.
item.dc:creator: Michela Eleuteri, Antonia Passarelli di Napoli

item.title: Growth of subsolutions to fully nonlinear equations in halfspaces II
item.description: arXiv:2611.27902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp lower growth estimates for subsolutions of fully nonlinear elliptic equations in half-spaces, allowing source terms that depend explicitly on the solution. The estimates capture both growth at infinity and blow-up at a finite distance from the boundary. Our approach extends the ODE-based method introduced in [J. Differential Equations 320 (2022), 143--173].
item.dc:creator: Fatma Gamze D\"uzg\"un, Niklas L. P. Lundstr\"om, Marcus Olofsson

item.title: Non autonomous problems with nearly linear growth and Orlicz-Sobolev coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.27903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the local Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers of non autonomous integral functionals of the form \[ \mathcal{F}(u, \Omega) = \int_\Omega F(x, Du)\, {\mathrm d}x, \] where $\Omega$ is a bounded open set of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 2$ and the energy density $F(x,\xi)$ satisfies nearly linear growth conditions with respect to the gradient variable. The main novelty of this work lies in the identification of a suitable quantitative balance between the logarithmic degeneration of the ellipticity and an Orlicz-Sobolev regularity of the partial map $x\to {F(x,\xi)}$ that is sufficient to obtain the Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers.
item.dc:creator: Michela Eleuteri, Antonia Passarelli di Napoli

item.title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
item.description: arXiv:2611.27940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.
item.dc:creator: Marta Menci, Marco Papi

item.title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II
item.description: arXiv:2611.27984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^\alpha\cap L_t^2H_x^{\alpha+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leq\alpha<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty. \] Thus non-uniqueness holds in optimal Sobolev spaces and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin weak spaces, even in a symmetry class where smooth solutions are globally regular. The proof relies on a computer-assisted construction of a linearly unstable forward self-similar solution, starting from the numerical profiles identified in our preceding paper (arXiv:2606.07501). We combine explicit asymptotic expansions and global residual estimates with weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals. Approximate solutions of auxiliary linear equations yield quantitative inverse bounds, allowing us to correct both the stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair by contraction arguments. The instability and localization theorem proved in arXiv:2606.07501 then produces the non-unique solutions.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Cadiot, Alexandru Ionescu, Hao Jia, Stan Palasek

item.title: Source Conditions and Sharp Transition Asymptotics for the Factorization Method with Far-Field Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.26778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The factorization method characterizes an obstacle through a range test, but practical implementations replace the associated Picard series by a regularized approximation. This paper studies the resulting regularization bias for inverse acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles. For a disc, we show that every positive-order H\"older source condition fails at each noncentral interior sampling point, whereas logarithmic source conditions hold uniformly on compact interior subsets for every exponent, with explicit constants. At the center, the bias decays linearly with the regularization parameter. We then derive sharp spectral transition asymptotics through the Lambert W function. These asymptotics determine the stabilization rate inside the obstacle, the iterated-logarithmic growth at the boundary, and the divergence outside. They also yield a threshold rule for which the reconstructed disc converges in measure, together with quantitative boundary-location estimates. For general impedance obstacles, we reduce the spectral decay of the symmetrized far-field operator to that of the data-to-pattern operator and obtain two-sided transition bounds in terms of the inradius and any radius larger than the circumradius. For a simply connected obstacle with analytic boundary, positive analytic impedance, and conformal center inside the obstacle, a Faber--Vekua normal form gives the sharp spectral law in terms of logarithmic capacity, with the same leading constant as for the disc. This class includes every convex analytic obstacle. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted spectral transition and illustrate its use in choosing the regularization level. The analytic normal-form result is proved only for a single boundary component.
item.dc:creator: George Pelekanos, Koung Hee Leem

item.title: Carleman estimates and $\phi$-null controllability for a fully discrete fourth-order parabolic equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a fully discrete approximation of a one-dimensional fourth-order parabolic equation with clamped boundary conditions, obtained by centered finite differences in space and the implicit Euler method in time, and controlled by two boundary controls acting at the left endpoint. We prove a Carleman estimate for the corresponding discrete adjoint operator, in which the large Carleman parameter is connected to the space and time discretization parameters $h$ and $\Delta t$. As a consequence, we obtain a relaxed observability inequality and a $\phi(h)$-null controllability result, in which the controls are bounded uniformly with respect to $h$ and $\Delta t$, and the norm of the solution at the final time is of order $\sqrt{\phi(h)}$, with $\phi(h)$ exponentially small, provided $\Delta t\le h^{\mu}$ for some $\mu\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: P\'ia Bizama, V\'ictor Hern\'andez-Santamar\'ia, Ariel A. P\'erez, Jose Solarte

item.title: Algebraic dark solitons versus rogue waves in the massive Thirring model
item.description: arXiv:2611.27045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We address the existence of algebraically decaying solitary waves on the nonzero wave background in the massive Thirring model (MTM) in laboratory coordinates. We find the precise condition of the spectral stability and instability of the nonzero wave background. In the case of instability, we distinguish modulational, side-band, and full-band instabilities and show that the rogue wave exists if and only if the nonzero wave background is modulationally unstable. For the other unstable cases and in the case of stability, we show that there exist exactly two algebraic dark solitons which correspond to the end points in the admissible range of the wave speed for the dark soliton propagation.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Zhao, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky

item.title: Weighted fixed-bidegree subelliptic estimates for the \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on Lipschitz pseudoconvex domain
item.description: arXiv:2611.27502v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish two types of \emph{a priori} subelliptic estimates for the twisted \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on a bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary. The estimates feature a subelliptic gain in \((0, 1/2)\) and are uniform with respect to the bidegree. The boundary is assumed to satisfy a plurisubharmonic-type condition, characterized by the local existence, near each boundary point, of a bounded plurisubharmonic function whose Hessian blows up algebraically near the boundary, with potentially different exponents at different points. The twisting function is holomorphic in a neighborhood of the domain, has bounded gradient, and its critical set inside the domain consists of isolated interior points with finite vanishing orders.
item.dc:creator: Ping'an Zhang

item.title: A proof of the polygonal Faber--Krahn inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.27968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every integer $n\ge3$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence, among simple polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides. We also obtain the optimal linear correction when fewer than $n$ sides are present. The proof combines a partition into convex cells with a mixed boundary comparison. Among convex polygons of fixed area and fixed sum of base angles less than $\pi$, the isosceles triangle minimizes the first eigenvalue with Dirichlet conditions on the base and Neumann conditions elsewhere. A comparison of Fourier transforms of conformal area densities proves this inequality and the corresponding upper bounds for inverse spectral moments of integer order at least two. We prove strict log-convexity of an interpolation of the eigenvalues of regular polygons of unit area for real parameters at least four. We then derive sharp hexagonal bounds for periodic convex polygonal tilings and asymptotic bounds for convex polygonal partitions of a fixed convex polygon, with an explicit correction for boundary junctions.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Li

item.title: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.27969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze a fully discrete finite element projection method for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and multiplicative noise. We show solvability and uniform moment estimates for the intermediate and the corrected velocity approximations under the assumption that the initial data is square-integrable and divergence free, and that the deterministic forcing term is bounded in $L^{q}(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ for a sufficiently large $q$. Under standard stability and approximation assumptions on the finite element spaces and a coupling condition on the spatial and temporal discretization parameters, we prove convergence of a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations. The analysis combines the complementary spatial and temporal estimates of the predicted and the corrected velocity approximations and uses the numerical dissipation to identify their common limit. We establish tightness of the piecewise constant temporal interpolations of the velocity field approximations using Aldous' criterion combined with the uniform discrete moment estimates. The convergence result holds in two and three space dimensions as it does not rely on any additional regularity of the limiting martingale solution beyond the one naturally available from the energy inequality. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the scheme in numerical experiments in two space dimensions for smooth and vortex sheet initial data.
item.dc:creator: Franziska Weber

item.title: Small scale quantum ergodicity in cat maps
item.description: arXiv:2005.00648v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study small scale quantum ergodicity in quantum cat maps, with semiclassical parameter 1/N, and prove three groups of results. First, for every N and every eigenbasis, almost all eigenstates are equidistributed on phase space balls of radius (log N)^(-a) for a<1/2, and on position space balls for a<1. For a set of N of full density and for Hecke eigenbases, almost all eigenstates, and even all of them, are equidistributed at polynomial scales. Second, every invariant probability measure is the semiclassical measure of quasimodes of order 1/log N, one for each N, that are not equidistributed at any scale between 4N^(-1/8) and a prescribed scale tending to zero. Third, there are orthonormal bases of quasimodes of order 1/log N for every N, and eigenbases for N with short periods, in which a full density subset is equidistributed at every fixed scale, but not at the scales (log N)^(-a) for a>1/2 in phase space and a>1 in position space. Hence, the exponents 1/2 and 1 in the first group are sharp: even for a full density subset of eigenstates, quantum ergodicity at fixed scales does not extend beyond the critical logarithmic scales.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong Han

item.title: Recovery guarantees for compressed sensing photoacoustic tomography
item.description: arXiv:2502.08846v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Photoacoustic tomography is an emerging medical imaging technology whose primary aim is to map the high-contrast optical properties of biological tissues by leveraging high-resolution ultrasound measurements. Mathematically, this can be framed as an inverse source problem for the wave equation over a specific domain. In this work, for the first time, it is shown how, by assuming signal sparsity, it is possible to establish rigorous stable recovery guarantees when the data collection is given by spatial averages restricted to a sparse, randomly sampled portion of the boundary. Our framework encompasses many approaches that have been considered in the literature. The result is a consequence of a general framework for subsampled inverse problems developed in previous works and refined stability estimates for an inverse problem for the wave equation with surface measurements.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Felisi

item.title: Strichartz estimates for the half Klein-Gordon equation on asymptotically flat backgrounds and applications to cubic Dirac equations
item.description: arXiv:2502.13670v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish the $L^2_t$-endpoint Strichartz estimate for (half) Klein-Gordon equations on a weakly asymptotically flat space-time. As an application we prove small data global well-posedness and scattering for massive cubic Dirac equations in the full subcritical range in this setting. Crucial ingredient is a parametrix contruction following the work of Metcalfe-Tataru and Xue and complements Strichartz estimates obtained by Zheng-Zhang. The proof of the global result for the cubic Dirac equation follows the strategy developed by Machihara-Nakanishi-Ozawa in the Euclidean setting.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Herr, Seokchang Hong

item.title: A P\"oschl--Teller approximation to the wave equation outside a torus
item.description: arXiv:2505.15264v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a short-time parametrix for the exterior Dirichlet wave equation on the complement of a solid torus. The construction involves freezing one coefficient of the conjugated Laplacian. This results in a family of radial P\"oschl--Teller equations. We bound the $L^2$ error in terms of the energy of the initial data. We then give several examples of Gaussian wavepackets in toroidal coordinates.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Quirchmayr, Alden Waters

item.title: Regularity for a strongly degenerate equation with explicit $u$-dependence
item.dc:creator: Miriam Piccirillo

item.title: Solution concepts for a model of visco-elasto-plasticity with slight compressibility
item.description: arXiv:2512.17464v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a model for the deformation of a visco-elasto-plastic material that is nearly incompressible. It originates from geophysics, is given in the Eulerian description and combines a Kelvin-Voigt rheology in the spherical part with a Jeffreys-type rheology in the deviatoric part. Despite a constant density, the model allows for non-isochoric deformation and the propagation of pressure waves. An additive decomposition of the strain rate into elastic and inelastic parts leads to an evolution equation for the small elastic strain, which is coupled with an adapted momentum equation. As plasticity is modeled through a non-smooth dissipation potential, we introduce a weak formulation in terms of a variational inequality. Since the well-posedness in such a weak setting is out of reach, we study two possible modifications: the regularization in terms of stress diffusion, and the relaxation of the solvability concept by transition to energy-variational solutions. In both cases, solutions are constructed by the same time-discrete scheme, consisting of solving a saddle-point problem in each time step.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Eiter

item.title: Existence and partial regularity of suitable weak solutions to the 3D Navier-Stokes-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equations
item.description: arXiv:2602.03131v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations coupled with the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation, which describes a two-phase mixture of the viscous incompressible fluid with particles or bubbles through a frictional force term. In the three-dimensional whole space, we construct a new class of suitable weak solutions to the Navier-Stokes-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck system satisfying energy estimates and three local or global energy inequalities of different forms. These obtained local energy inequalities play an important role in characterizing the measure of the singularity set of weak solutions. The main difficulties in deriving these inequalities lie in establishing the convergence of the density function $f$ in bounded or unbounded domains and dealing with the convergence of the non-local frictional force term. The strong $L^1$ convergence of $|v|^k f$ for $0\le k<\kappa$ and of $|v|^k f\log f$ locally in $x$ for $0\le k<\kappa/2$ is proved by using new a priori estimates for the velocity, Tao's $L^p$ decomposition, and the DiPerna-Lions compactness method. Moreover, as an immediate consequence of the existence result, we are able to describe the Hausdorff dimension of set of singular points of the fluid velocity $u$ and also establish the $\alpha$-H\"{o}lder continuity of $f$ at the regular points of $u$.
item.dc:creator: Renjun Duan, Fengqiang Shi, Wendong Wang, Jianbo Yu

item.title: A Fujita-type threshold for the semilinear damped wave equation with Hartree-type nonlinearity and initial data from homogeneous Besov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.23764v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the semilinear damped wave equation with Hartree-type nonlinearity $\mathcal{I}_\gamma(|u|^{p_1})|u|^{p_2}$, where $0<\gamma<n$, and initial data possessing additional negative regularity in $\dot{B}_{2,\infty}^{-\beta}$, $0\leq\beta<n/2$. We first establish decay estimates for the corresponding linear equation in homogeneous Besov spaces $\dot{B}_{q,r}^s$, allowing low-frequency data in $\dot{B}_{m,\infty}^{-\beta}$ under the condition $s+\beta+n(1/m-1/q)>0$. We then prove the existence of a unique global mild solution for sufficiently small initial data in the critical and supercritical range $$ p_1+p_2\geq1+\frac{4+2\gamma}{n+2\beta}, $$ under the remaining assumptions on $p_1$ and $p_2$. Furthermore, for initial data satisfying a positive lower bound, we prove the nonexistence of global weak solutions when $$ 2<p_1+p_2<1+\frac{4+2\gamma}{n+2\beta}. $$
item.dc:creator: Thuy Hien Thi Nguyen, Duc An Phan

item.title: A pathological set regarding the propagation of almost sure properties of Gaussian measures
item.description: arXiv:2605.31359v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a complementary result to the quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures supported on Sobolev spaces with high regularity under the dynamics of the three-dimensional periodic defocusing nonlinear wave equation from Gunaratnam-Oh-Tzvetkov-Weber (2022). Namely, given $p > 2$, $\sigma$ large enough and $\alpha \in [\max\{\frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{p} , 0\} , 1 - \frac{2}{p})$, we prove the existence of dense subsets of the Sobolev space $W^{\sigma + \alpha,p}(\mathbb{T}^3)$ which do not preserve the $L^p$-based regularity $\sigma$ throughout the aforementioned dynamics. This is in sharp contrast with the propagation under the flow of almost sure properties.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Merino

item.title: Minnaert resonances and higher-order acoustic modes for bubbles in a viscous fluid with surface tension
item.description: arXiv:2606.21070v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the low-frequency resonances (Minnaert resonances) for micro-bubbles in a viscous fluid with surface tension. The interior pressure is coupled to the exterior pressure--velocity system through a normal hydrodynamic Neumann-to-Dirichlet operator. We analyze the incompressible limit of this operator and its coupling to the linearized curvature operator. This coupling introduces an additional non-resonance condition needed to isolate the low-frequency acoustic modes considered here. Under this non-resonance condition, we derive leading-order asymptotic formulas for the resonant frequencies in terms of the difference in the acoustic impedance at the interface between the gas and the fluid. For multiple bubbles, the collective resonances are governed by an effective capacitance matrix. The spherical calculation recovers the known viscosity and surface-tension corrections. Possible extensions to higher-order resonances, i.e., beyond the subwavelength regime, are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Habib Ammari, Xin Fu, Wenjia Jing, Hongjie Li

item.title: Existence of weak solutions of the surface Beris-Edwards model
item.description: arXiv:2607.01638v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of weak solutions to the surface Beris-Edwards model for nematic liquid crystals posed on a $d$-dimensional ($d \in \{2,3\}$) closed hypersurface of class $C^{2,1}$. This thermodynamically consistent model, recently introduced by Bouck, Nochetto and Yushutin (2024), couples the incompressible tangent Navier-Stokes equations with a kinematic equation for the Q-tensor field that encodes the orientation of the liquid crystal particles with a general state of orientational order. Extending ideas by Abels, Dolzmann and Liu (2014) and Guill\'en-Gonz\'alez and Rodr\'iguez-Bellido (2015) for the Beris-Edwards model in flat domains, we design a Faedo-Galerkin scheme based upon eigenfunctions of an appropriate tangent Stokes operator and tensor-valued Laplace-Beltrami operator and recover a weak solution via standard compactness arguments.
item.dc:creator: Gonzalo A. Benavides, Ricardo H. Nochetto, Mansur Shakipov

item.title: An indefinite Coulomb interaction from the Steklov spectrum of perforated manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.25211v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates for Steklov eigenvalues and harmonically extended eigenfunctions toward their weighted Laplace--Beltrami counterparts on a closed manifold perforated by many small geodesic balls. The holes have radii that scale critically with respect to their spacing in the sense that the boundary area of each hole balances with the weighted volume of its Voronoi cell. We then derive a higher-order expansion of the Steklov eigenvalues; in dimensions two and three, we identify two correction scales. The expansion is governed by an indefinite Coulomb-type energy of the discrepancy between the boundary and bulk measures, mediated by the reduced Green function of the limiting operator. The proof relies on sharp estimates for certain auxiliary functions that we introduce in order to quantify the discrepancy measure between the surface measure on the holes and their background density. Our paper serves to bridge an emerging literature in spectral geometry with one on systems of points interacting via Coulomb-type energies.
item.dc:creator: Zhonggan Huang, Raghavendra Venkatraman

item.title: Orlicz space relaxation of total variation denoising
item.description: arXiv:2609.26645v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider variational image denoising with spatially dependent Orlicz regularization and introduce an Orlicz--Sobolev approximation of the ROF model based on a scaled $L\log L$-type density. For a general class of uniformly superlinear integrands satisfying a $\Delta_2$-condition, we establish existence and uniqueness of minimizers and derive a Fenchel dual problem with dual attainment and pointwise optimality conditions. We then specialize the framework to a logarithmic density whose correction is activated above a prescribed local gradient scale. For this model, we obtain explicit expressions of the Fenchel dual and optimality conditions as well as a pointwise radial formula for the dual proximal map involving the Lambert $W$-function. As the logarithmic parameter tends to zero, we prove equicoercivity and $\Gamma$-convergence to the ROF functional, together with convergence of the corresponding minimizers. Numerical illustrations indicate that the logarithmic correction can reduce staircasing for diffuse transitions, while retaining behavior comparable to ROF for sharp interfaces and a natural image.
item.dc:creator: Christian Clason, Tobias Unterberger

item.title: Global Regularity for the Chemotaxis-Stokes System with Signal Consumption in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2609.35204v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the continuum model of aerobic bacteria proposed by Tuval et al. in 2005, we study the large-data regularity problem for the three-dimensional chemotaxis--Stokes system with signal consumption. We prove the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^3$ for smooth initial data with finite density mass and moment and finite signal Fisher information, without any smallness assumptions. The proof is based on three main ideas. First, we use a terminal heat-kernel representation to define a finite signal value at every spatial point and prove strong $L^a$ convergence of the backward parabolic signal rescalings to this value for every $1\le a<\infty$. Second, we prove a localized entropy estimate that remains uniform under density normalization, even when the resulting consumption coefficient becomes arbitrarily large. These estimates give two complementary mechanisms: consumption excludes normalized density concentration at points with positive terminal signal, while a localized weighted estimate improves density integrability at points with zero terminal signal. Third, we establish a local $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion based on smallness of scale-invariant density, velocity, and pressure quantities. A heat decomposition recovers the required signal-gradient smallness, removing it as a separate assumption. Together, these yield the decay of a scale-invariant density quantity and then exclude finite-time singularities.
item.dc:creator: Fengqiang Shi, Wendong Wang, Guoxu Yang

item.title: Decoupling and Tail Laws for Small-Order Metric-Valued Nonlocal Energies: A Structural View of the Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova Formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.01958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for small-order limits of nonlocal energies with metric-valued maps. For globally $L^p$ maps, we consider interaction measures whose marginals have uniformly bounded $L^\infty$ densities $a_\alpha$ and $b_\alpha$. If these densities converge weakly-* to $a_\infty$ and $b_\infty$, the normalized energies converge to the $L^p$ energy weighted by $a_\infty+b_\infty$ if and only if the interaction measures escape every bounded rectangle. For maps that are only locally $L^p$, we introduce target laws describing the distribution of the values sampled at infinity. Convergence of their $p$-distance profiles yields the limiting interaction energy for every $1\leq p<\infty$ and arbitrary Polish targets, with integrated $p$-Wasserstein convergence as a sufficient criterion. The arguments include the endpoint $p=1$ and require no linear structure on the target space. Applications include directional and anisotropic Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova formulas, a Bernoulli-law interpretation of fractional perimeters, and an Abelian principle for heat-semigroup energies.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Pinamonti

item.title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
item.description: arXiv:2610.34048v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Hidekazu Yoshioka, Motoh Tsujimura, Ayumi Hashiguchi

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37423v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the sharp bound $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$ for the threefold additive energy of every lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, with an absolute constant. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ estimate for eigenfunctions on $\mathbb{T}^2$, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical uniform $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and confirms Bourgain's conjecture in this range. For all $k\ge4$, we obtain the fixed power saving for the $k$-fold additive energy $J_k(P_n)\le C|P_n|^{2k-3-\delta}$, with absolute constants $C,\delta>0$. Applications include mean-square convergence of observables and the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Liouville systems I: Blow-up analysis and orthogonal decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.07857v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study blow-up solutions of generalized Liouville systems on a closed surface at and near critical parameter hypersurfaces. Under a Morse assumption on the reduced functional, we establish the following results. First, we introduce amplitude variables in the approximate manifold and prove that every sequence of blow-up solutions at a fixed critical parameter, or along an admissible sequence from the lower side, admits a unique minimizing decomposition up to permutation. The remainder converges to zero and is orthogonal to the center, scale, and amplitude directions. The concentration scales are comparable, the limiting configuration satisfies the scale balance conditions, and the amplitudes vanish after multiplication by the logarithmic scale. Second, we determine the leading parameter defect in both critical decay regimes and prove that, along each fixed admissible path, all sufficiently large solutions lie in finitely many disjoint bubbling neighborhoods. Finally, assuming the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical configuration, the solution set at the fixed critical parameter is compact. These results provide the analytic foundation for studying the resonant degree via critical points at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Mohameden Ahmedou, Jonas Fey, Zhengni Hu, Lei Zhang

item.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
item.description: arXiv:2611.14315v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lema\^{i}tre--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.
item.dc:creator: Xueyi Yu

item.title: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.19067v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_\tau:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Z\tau)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_{\tau}(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_{\tau}$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given. In particular, we resolve a conjecture of Luo and Wei (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 2022).
item.dc:creator: Zhijie Chen, Chen-Gang Long, Shihong Zhang

item.title: Global renormalized finite-energy weak solutions to the three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system on tori for $\gamma>4/3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.25843v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Building on the foundational theory of finite-energy weak solutions initiated by P.-L. Lions and further developed by E. Feireisl and collaborators, we establish the global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, with constant viscosity coefficients and pressure law \(P(\rho)=\rho^\gamma\), for every \(\gamma>4/3\) and arbitrary finite-energy initial data. This extends the classical three-dimensional Lions--Feireisl existence theory beyond the threshold \(\gamma>3/2\), and in particular, covers the important case $ \gamma=7/5 $ for air (cf. \cite{Anderson}). Compared to the classical theory, we develop a novel approach to establish the improved pressure-integrability estimate compatible with the viscous and inertial terms, via constructing a periodic test field through barycentric optimal transport. This improved pressure-integrability estimate, combined with an effective viscous flux identity and an entropy comparison, provides the compactness needed to identify the nonlinear limits and recover the energy inequality.
item.dc:creator: Guangyi Hong, Hongyun Peng, Changjiang Zhu

item.title: Combined effects of evaporation, sedimentation and solute crystallization on the dynamics of aerosol size distributions on multiple length and time scales
item.description: arXiv:2601.05876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate three aspects of aerosol-mediated air-borne viral infection mechanisms on different length and time scales. First, we address the evolution of the size distribution of a non-interacting ensemble of droplets that are subject to evaporation and sedimentation using a sharp droplet-air interface model. From the exact solution of the evolution equation we derive the viral load in the air and show that it depends sensitively on the relative humidity. Secondly, from Molecular Dynamics simulations we extract the molecular reflection coefficient of single water molecules from the air-water interface. This parameter determines the water condensation and evaporation rate at a liquid droplet surface and therefore the evaporation rate of aqueous droplets. We find the reflection of water to be negligible at room temperature but to rise significantly at elevated temperatures and for grazing incidence angles. Thirdly, we derive a thermodynamically consistent three-dimensional diffuse-interface model for solute-containing droplets that is formulated as a three-phase Cahn-Hilliard/Allen-Cahn system. By numerically solving the coupled system of equations, we explore representative scenarios that show that this model reproduces and generalizes features of the sharp-interface model. These interconnected studies on the dynamics of aerosol droplet evaporation are relevant in order to quantitatively assess the airborne infection risk under varying environmental conditions.
item.dc:creator: Sina Zendehroud, Ole Kleinjung, Philip Loche, Lyd\'eric Bocquet, Roland R. Netz, Erica Ipocoana, Dirk Peschka, Marita Thomas

item.title: Torsional Rigidity and Spherical Deficit for a Dirichlet Problem on Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2605.30088v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we study several inequalities related to a Dirichlet problem on Riemannian manifolds whose Ricci curvature is bounded from below. First, we establish sharp inequalities involving the torsional rigidity and show that equality forces the domain to be isometric to a geodesic ball in a space form, with no symmetry assumption on the ambient manifold. Next, we derive an integral identity associated with the same Dirichlet problem, which measures the spherical deficit arising in this context. In particular, we apply this identity to Einstein manifolds, where it yields a rigidity result and a bound for the weighted spherical deficit in terms of the deviation of the normal derivative from a constant.
item.dc:creator: Maria Andrade, Allan Freitas

item.title: Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.31271v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon, and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_{1}$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen, Kuangmiao Xiong, Boxi Xu

item.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.17625v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.
item.dc:creator: Richard Duong, Janis Auffenberg, Gabriele Steidl
